CARES Architecture Reconciliation Changelog

Date: 2026-11-21
Status: Documentation reconciliation and technical decision preparation only (NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT TESTED). No application code, schema, DDL, migrations, or tests were created or modified.

Purpose

Record documentation changes made to address findings in ARCHITECTURE_CROSS_DOCUMENT_CONSISTENCY_REVIEW.md and to prepare a consistent baseline for formal PostgreSQL schema design review.

Mandatory constraints preserved

The reconciliation preserves:

  • Python backend.
  • PostgreSQL as the authoritative primary relational system of record.
  • One unique monitored device equals exactly one licensed asset.
  • Multiple data sources/connectors reporting the same physical/logical monitored device must not create duplicate licensed assets.
  • Asset licensing is separate from technical resource quotas.
  • External SaaS AI providers only; no local AI/GPU infrastructure.
  • CARES core must operate independently of MELIRA.
  • Existing product roadmap and commercial decisions were not altered.

ADR governance and decision integrity

  • ADR 0006: status preserved as Proposed (not silently changed to Accepted). Reconciliation edits were limited to justified clarifications/cross-references and did not resolve owner decisions.
  • Owner decisions: no commercial, privacy, legal, security, or operational owner decision was silently resolved. Pending decisions remain explicitly listed in POSTGRESQL_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md and reconciled source docs where relevant.
  • Proposed controls: reconciled controls/designs remain NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT TESTED unless actual repository evidence proves otherwise. No security validation is claimed from documentation.

Remaining contradictions / gaps after reconciliation

  • docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_PACKAGE_FINAL_CORRECTIONS.md contains detailed illustrative designs that remain proposals; reconciled source docs intentionally cross-reference rather than duplicate them. Formal schema/security review must still select concrete mechanisms (binding implementation, exact policy catalog, DDL/constraints, definer/grant matrix).
  • Exact table/column names, uniqueness tuples, RLS policy definitions, idempotency ledger schema, and outbox class/schema split are not finalized.
  • Some operational details (provider reconciliation contracts, evidence storage/WORM commitments, retention/legal-hold specifics, performance/SLO commitments) remain unresolved by owner/security/integration decisions.
  • No new contradictions were intentionally introduced by reconciliation edits; however, final authority for unresolved technical selections rests with formal design review and owner/security approvals.

Readiness statement

The documentation baseline is more consistent after reconciliation but not yet fully ready for final/approved formal PostgreSQL schema design as an unambiguous implemented specification. It is suitable for preparatory/formal schema-design review provided TD-001–TD-009, the operation-by-operation transaction-boundary map, and unresolved owner decisions are explicitly tracked and resolved/accepted as required.
